_fixture: what .claude/skills/apply-job/scan-page.js produces for pages/ashby-remounted.html — GENERATED by running the real scanner over the served page (POST to the Ashby route), never hand-written
_bridge: tests/security/scan-fidelity.test.mjs runs the REAL scanner over that HTML and deep-compares this file to its output. Edit one and the other goes red.
_why: THE REMOUNT LEG. Ashby replaces the form subtree ~700ms after a resume is chosen. Before this fixture the post-remount DOM existed nowhere a test without a browser could reach, so every no-browser leg measured the PRE-remount form and labelled it Ashby. `bench-apply.mjs --board ashby --page 2` now resolves this, and the re-scan and re-fill a remount forces can be costed offline. Phase 0.10.
_diff_from_step1: The ONLY differences are f2/f3/f4 acquiring `v` — the values the board's resume parser wrote — and the status node's text (which is not a field). Field set, labels, order, `k` stamps, combo and buttons are identical, on purpose: a remount that also changed the questions would let a real bug hide behind an expected difference.
_what_a_scan_cannot_show: The hazard the remount actually causes is INVISIBLE here, and that is worth saying out loud. Every element identity is new and every data-aj stamp is gone, so every handle the filler holds is stale — but a scan describes a DOM, not the history of one, so this file and step 1 differ only in three values. The staleness is asserted where it is observable: tests/security/board-fidelity.test.mjs checks the served bytes, and fill-engine.mjs's actOn/isStaleError retry is what pays for it.
_v_provenance: f2/f3/f4 carry values THE AGENT DID NOT SUPPLY — the board wrote them. A filler that reads 'already has a value' as 'I filled this' is reading its own success off a third party's write, and on a hostile board those bytes are the attacker's.
